name: Journey to the West: The Flaming Mountains (ch. 59-61)
campaignName: Journey to the West: The Flaming Mountains (ch. 59-61)
description: Three chapters of Wu Cheng'en's Xiyou ji (Yu translation, checked against the Chinese): borrowing the palm-leaf fan from Rakshasi, the Bull Demon King's two households, the transformation contest and the net of Heaven and Earth, and the forty-nine waves that quench the Mountain of Flames. 9 quests, 21 NPCs, 7 factions, 12 relics, 5 clocks, 6 bestiary entries across 4 maps.
author: Campaign Converter (Claude)

npcs.name: Tripitaka (Tang Monk)
npcs.role: Scripture pilgrim; leader of the party
npcs.motivation: Reach the Western Heaven for the scriptures without turning aside; he will not accept a detour even when the road is fire.

secretsKnown.secret: He is afraid of the heat and the fire, and silently doubts the journey can proceed; he hides it behind duty.
secretsKnown.revealCondition: If a second failed attempt leaves him alone with Sha Monk by the road.

dialogueHooks: Soft-spoken, formal; addresses each disciple by a Buddhist name (Wukong, Wuneng, Wujing).
Under pressure he refuses to be moved from the West: 'I only want to go where the scriptures are.'
Crucible reaction: when all four are in danger he sends the disciple least able to refuse, then thanks each by name afterwards.

relationships.notes: Trusts him as eldest disciple though he fears his violence.

npcs.notes: **Want:** Cross the mountain and keep going West. **Need:** To accept that borrowing the fan is a trial of mind and not merely of strength. **Wound:** Every obstacle has cost him tears; the road keeps asking him to trust disciples whose past he knows.

leverage.vulnerability: Thirst, heat and fear of being left alone by the road.
leverage.bribe: Reassurance that merit is nearly complete and the mission is blessed.
leverage.threat: Abandonment by the disciples or a failed crossing ends the mission.

npcs.faction: The Tang Pilgrim Party

npcs.name: Sun Wukong, the Great Sage
npcs.motivation: Bring the real fan back to his master and avoid killing the Bull King, who was once a sworn brother.

secretsKnown.secret: He swallowed the Wind-Arresting Elixir by accident and does not know it keeps him immune to the fan for the rest of the arc.
secretsKnown.revealCondition: When the Bull King's fan fails to move him during his climactic mountain duel and he recognises the pellet.

secretsKnown.secret: He never asked Rakshasi how to shrink the fan and can only carry it on his shoulder.
secretsKnown.revealCondition: As soon as he tries to shrink it after leaving the cave.

dialogueHooks: Teasing, kinship-first speech: 'sister-in-law', 'eldest brother'; he opens every meeting with a bow and a joke.
Under pressure he drops the pose, grows enormous and uses the rod.
Crucible reaction: refuses to kill kin; prefers to trick, humiliate and bargain.

relationships.notes: Needles him but depends on him in battle.
Red Boy's mother; he addresses her as sister-in-law.
Once one of seven sworn brothers.
Helped in the Yellow Wind affair; now supplies the elixir.
The spirit's account of his own past shakes him.

npcs.notes: **Want:** The real fan without a killing. **Need:** To accept that his old actions (the brazier, Red Boy) created this fire. **Wound:** His past shames him; each enemy is a consequence of an earlier act.

leverage.vulnerability: Pride in his own tricks; he trusts a familiar face (Bajie) without checking.
leverage.bribe: Flattery of his transformations and of the old brotherhood of seven.

npcs.faction: The Tang Pilgrim Party

npcs.name: Zhu Eight Rules
npcs.motivation: A comfortable passage; he first urges finding another road, then turns savage once his rake is in his hands.

secretsKnown.secret: He fears the Bull King's reputation and is only brave when the local spirit and ghost soldiers back him.
secretsKnown.revealCondition: When he first meets the Bull King's guards without allies.

dialogueHooks: Grumbling, food-first speech; calls Wukong 'Elder Brother' even when he disagrees.
Under pressure he whirls the rake wildly and shouts abuse.
Crucible reaction: suggests going home, then does the work.

relationships.notes: The spirit leads him to Hoard-Thunder.
He kills her in one blow.

npcs.notes: **Want:** An easy road. **Need:** To prove that he matters in a fight. **Wound:** Wukong's contempt.

leverage.vulnerability: Hunger, comfort and the opinion of his elder brother.
leverage.bribe: Food, rest and a share of credit.

npcs.faction: The Tang Pilgrim Party

npcs.name: Sha Monk (Wujing)
npcs.motivation: Keep the Master safe and the luggage whole; he is the one who names the dilemma without panicking.
dialogueHooks: Quiet, short sentences; names a problem and then waits.
Under pressure he guards the Master's side without leaving.
Crucible reaction: recognises the divine warriors by name and bows first.
npcs.notes: **Want:** The Master safe. **Need:** To be asked for his judgement. **Wound:** Being the quiet one.

leverage.vulnerability: His loyalty is total; he would not abandon Tripitaka alone.
leverage.bribe: Tasks that keep him close to the Master.

npcs.faction: The Tang Pilgrim Party

npcs.name: The Old Householder (Gonggong)
npcs.role: Village elder of the red-brick homes
npcs.motivation: Keep the households fed and honour the fan's rules; he insists the visitors bring proper gifts.

secretsKnown.secret: No one in the village has ever seen the fan's keeper; the tribute is paid on trust.
secretsKnown.revealCondition: If the party asks to see a household record of the decennial audience.

dialogueHooks: Courteous, wary; half-startled by the strangers at first, then lavish.
Under pressure he reminds the party of the tribute: four hogs, four sheep, flowers, fruit, fowl, wine.
Crucible reaction: offers dried food and two companions for a road without houses.
npcs.notes: **Want:** Rain. **Need:** A reason to trust visitors. **Wound:** Decades of reliance on a power he cannot meet.

leverage.vulnerability: His region will starve without rain.
leverage.bribe: Rain, safe passage, an end to the fire.
leverage.threat: Removal of the fan or a second fire from the pilgrims' meddling.

npcs.faction: The Households of the Mountain of Flames and the Local Spirit Office

npcs.name: The Rice-Pudding Peddler
npcs.motivation: Sell hot puddings and keep his trade alive; he knows the fan is the source of his flour.
dialogueHooks: Sing-song street hawker chant: 'Steaming cakes! Hot millet cakes! If you want flour, consult Iron-Fan's power; if you want grain, bring her sheep and swine!'
When questioned on the Flaming Mountains: wipes sweat with a soiled cloth: 'You strangers seek the West? Turn back! Even iron boots turn to bubbling soup on that mountain.'
Crucible roleplaying cue: Eagerly accepts silver coin to point out the local spirit's shrine, but bolts behind his brick stove the moment divine weapons are drawn.
npcs.notes: **Want:** Sales. **Need:** Regular rain. **Wound:** Burnt fingers.
npcs.faction: The Households of the Mountain of Flames and the Local Spirit Office

npcs.name: The Woodcutter of Jade Cloud Mountain
npcs.motivation: Send travellers safely to the cave and persuade them not to carry old grudges.
dialogueHooks: Singing, unhurried; chants of forest paths and rain.
Under pressure he smiles and gives directions.
Crucible reaction: tells Wukong to borrow the fan with no grudge.

relationships.notes: Calms him before the first duel.

npcs.notes: **Want:** A quiet forest. **Need:** To be heard.

leverage.bribe: Courtesy and a plain request for directions.

npcs.faction: The Households of the Mountain of Flames and the Local Spirit Office

npcs.name: Local Spirit of the Mountain of Flames
npcs.role: Banished furnace attendant and mountain's tutelary deity
npcs.motivation: Win a pardon from Laozi by helping quench the fire, then stay to care for the people.

secretsKnown.secret: The fire began with bricks from Laozi's brazier, and Wukong himself kicked them loose.
secretsKnown.revealCondition: When Wukong accepts that the fan he borrowed is false.

dialogueHooks: Humble, formal; dressed as a Daoist, calls Eight Rules 'Heavenly Reeds'.
Under pressure he reminds gods and demons of Heaven's protection for the scripture journey.
Crucible reaction: refuses to let the party find another way; calls it 'heterodoxy'.
npcs.notes: **Want:** A pardon. **Need:** To be relieved of his post honourably. **Wound:** Laozi banished him for carelessness.

leverage.vulnerability: He is in exile and needs a pardon.
leverage.threat: Heaven's displeasure if the fire is not quenched.

npcs.faction: The Households of the Mountain of Flames and the Local Spirit Office

npcs.name: Rakshasi, Princess Iron-Fan
npcs.role: Keeper of the palm-leaf fan; Bull King's wife; mother of Red Boy
npcs.motivation: Avenge Red Boy's fall and keep her husband and her fan; she refuses to lend the fan until her son is returned.

secretsKnown.secret: The true fan is kept in her mouth as an almond-leaf; the shrink spell is separate.
secretsKnown.revealCondition: If she is drunk or addressed as the Bull King.

secretsKnown.secret: Forty-nine waves quench the mountain forever.

dialogueHooks: Cold, formal; calls Wukong 'wretched ape' first, 'brother-in-law' once he hurts her.
Under pressure she bargains: 'a treasure is not lent lightly'.
Crucible reaction: yields only when Heaven surrounds the cave.
npcs.notes: **Want:** Her son back and her husband home. **Need:** To let both go and attend to her own cultivation. **Wound:** The Bull King left her for a fox-king's heiress and sends money in his place.

leverage.vulnerability: Love for her husband and pain at his desertion; wine.
leverage.bribe: Red Boy's return or a visit.

npcs.faction: The Palm-Leaf Cave Household

npcs.name: The Palm-Leaf Cave Gate Maid
npcs.motivation: Serve Rakshasi faithfully; announce guests and hold the fan when asked.
dialogueHooks: Clipped, strict palace etiquette: 'State your name and offering, traveler. No male person—not even a suckling child—sets foot beyond this gate.'
Under interrogation or celestial threat: clutches her floral basket defensively, backing away toward the inner courtyard screaming for Princess Iron-Fan.
Crucible roleplaying cue: Whispers terrified warnings that the fan is a fiery decoy if Sun Wukong threatens her life, pleading to be spared.
npcs.notes: **Want:** Order. **Need:** A gentler mistress.
npcs.faction: The Palm-Leaf Cave Household

npcs.name: Bull Demon King (King Powerful)
npcs.role: Great demon king of the West; consort to two households
npcs.motivation: Avenge his son and the insult to both wives, and keep the fan from the monkey.

secretsKnown.secret: He can shrink the true fan; Wukong cannot.
secretsKnown.revealCondition: When he takes the fan from Wukong while disguised as Eight Rules.

secretsKnown.secret: He is the 'world-wrecker' only in name; he is vain and indulgent with his concubine.
secretsKnown.revealCondition: If he is baited with gossip about Jade Countenance.

dialogueHooks: Blunt, proud; addresses Wukong as 'monkey' but 'bond-brother' if cornered.
Under pressure he changes shape: swan, eagle, crane, deer, leopard, bear, bull.
Crucible reaction: refuses to give the fan; 'the fan's a small thing, but my hatred is deep'.
npcs.notes: **Want:** Revenge and to keep both households. **Need:** To accept that his son is safe and that his wives need separate attention. **Wound:** Red Boy's capture by Guanyin.

leverage.vulnerability: His son and both households; a banquet invitation.
leverage.bribe: A friend's invitation or news of Red Boy.
leverage.threat: Heaven's decree and the Four Guardians.

npcs.faction: The Hoard-Thunder Court of the Bull Demon King

npcs.name: Princess Jade Countenance
npcs.role: Heiress of the fox-king's fortune; Bull King's concubine
npcs.motivation: Protect her home and the husband she bought with her wealth; she wants Rakshasi out of his thoughts.

secretsKnown.secret: She is a fox spirit; her true form is a white-faced fox.
secretsKnown.revealCondition: When she is struck down by Eight Rules.

dialogueHooks: Furious, theatrical; weeps, stamps and demands protection.
Under pressure she summons the external guard.
Crucible reaction: asks the Bull King to kill the monkey.
npcs.notes: **Want:** Security. **Need:** A husband she has not bought. **Wound:** Orphaned; she gave her father's fortune to secure protection.
npcs.faction: The Hoard-Thunder Court of the Bull Demon King

npcs.name: Captain of the Cloud-Touching Cave's External Guard
npcs.motivation: Hold the door and report intruders.
dialogueHooks: Trembling, frantic report: 'My Lord! My Lady! A hairy-faced thunder-demon with an iron rod has broken into the orchid pines and frightened the young mistress into weeping!'
Under pressure or ambush: brandishes his heavy steel spear with shaky bravado, threatening to strike the bronze gong to summon the hundred-strong beast guard.
Crucible roleplaying cue: If Jade Countenance falls in battle, drops his spear and flees into the southern wilderness; if the Bull King commands, charges fearlessly into the melee.
npcs.notes: **Want:** Survive the day. **Need:** A safer post.
npcs.faction: The Hoard-Thunder Court of the Bull Demon King

npcs.name: The Old Dragon King of the Green Wave Lagoon
npcs.role: Lord of the lagoon court; banquet host
npcs.motivation: Preside over a flawless banquet; he is gracious until a breach of etiquette threatens his guests.
dialogueHooks: Formal, courtly; asks 'where did you come from, wild crab?'
Under pressure he orders flogging, then accepts the court's intercession.
Crucible reaction: tells the Bull King to avoid offending Wukong on the road to the West.
npcs.notes: **Want:** A seamless banquet. **Need:** To keep out of the Bull King's feud.

leverage.vulnerability: A court that depends on appearances.

npcs.faction: The Green Wave Lagoon Court

npcs.name: Bodhisattva Lingji
npcs.role: Bodhisattva of Little Sumeru; former subduer of the Yellow Wind fiend
npcs.motivation: Help the Tang Monk by affinity and return to his temple; he has no time to entertain.

secretsKnown.secret: The elixir was never used before; Tathagata gave it for exactly this fan.
secretsKnown.revealCondition: Wukong asks how the Master can overcome the hurdle.

dialogueHooks: Calm, friendly; asks first whether the scriptures are obtained.
Under pressure he stays calm and gives instructions.
Crucible reaction: sends Wukong back with the elixir sewn in.
npcs.notes: **Want:** The journey completed. **Need:** To hand over what he holds.
npcs.faction: The Little Sumeru Temple

npcs.name: Devaraja Li, the Pagoda-Bearer
npcs.role: Celestial general acting on the Jade Emperor's decree
npcs.motivation: Carry out the Jade Emperor's decree; hold the mirror steady until the Bull King yields.
dialogueHooks: Formal, curt; 'by decree of the Jade Emperor, we are here to arrest you'.
Under pressure he trains the mirror and says nothing.
Crucible reaction: hands the spoils to the Buddha's order.
npcs.notes: **Want:** The arrest completed. **Need:** To keep his son's methods lawful.
npcs.faction: The Heavenly and Buddhist Enforcement Host

npcs.name: Third Prince Nata
npcs.motivation: Take the bull in his three-headed form and accept its surrender.
dialogueHooks: Bright, confident; 'Great Sage, watch me capture him'.
Under pressure he multiplies arms and heads.
Crucible reaction: ties the bull with his rope and leads him to Buddha.
npcs.notes: **Want:** A clean capture. **Need:** To avoid killing a surrendering foe.
npcs.faction: The Heavenly and Buddhist Enforcement Host

npcs.name: Diamond Guardian Dharma Diffusion
npcs.motivation: Hold the north quarter of the cosmic net for Sakyamuni.
dialogueHooks: Resounding, metallic baritone echoing like bronze bells: 'By decree of Sakyamuni Tathagata, the Northern Cosmic Net is cast! Bull Demon King, your reincarnation as a brute ends today!'
Under combat escalation: extends golden diamond chains across the sky, anchoring the cosmic perimeter of the North.
Crucible roleplaying cue: Stands impassive as a mountain bastion, refusing parley or mortal bribery until Prince Nata accepts the beast's surrender.
npcs.notes: **Want:** Hold the north quarter at the Cliff of Mysterious Demons so the bull cannot run toward the Mountain of Five Platforms. **Role:** First of the four guardians to challenge the fleeing Bull King.
npcs.faction: The Heavenly and Buddhist Enforcement Host

npcs.name: Diamond Guardian Victorious Ultimate
npcs.motivation: Hold the south quarter by the Buddha's decree.
dialogueHooks: Thunderous, unyielding command: 'The Southern gate of Heaven is barred by the Victorious Diamond Guardian! Yield to the Western pilgrimage or be ground beneath Mount Sumeru!'
Under combat escalation: extends golden diamond chains across the sky, anchoring the cosmic perimeter of the South.
Crucible roleplaying cue: Stands impassive as a mountain bastion, refusing parley or mortal bribery until Prince Nata accepts the beast's surrender.
npcs.notes: **Want:** Hold the south quarter from the Pure-Cool Cave of Emei Mountain, closing the road when the Bull King doubles back. **Role:** Second guardian to block him, by decree of the Buddha.
npcs.faction: The Heavenly and Buddhist Enforcement Host

npcs.name: Diamond Guardian Great Strength
npcs.motivation: Hold the east quarter by Tathagata's secret command.
dialogueHooks: Earth-shaking celestial roar: 'Tathagata's secret writ commands your capture! The Eastern quarter is sealed; no swan nor tiger slips through our Diamond phalanx!'
Under combat escalation: extends golden diamond chains across the sky, anchoring the cosmic perimeter of the East.
Crucible roleplaying cue: Stands impassive as a mountain bastion, refusing parley or mortal bribery until Prince Nata accepts the beast's surrender.
npcs.notes: **Want:** Hold the east quarter from Ear-Touching Ridge on Sumeru Mountain. **Role:** Third guardian; a Vaisravana ascetic who acts on Tathagata's secret command rather than a public decree.
npcs.faction: The Heavenly and Buddhist Enforcement Host

npcs.name: Diamond Guardian Ever Abiding
npcs.motivation: Hold the west quarter by the personal order of the aged Buddha.
dialogueHooks: Deep, ancient vibration: 'The aged Buddha orders the Western quadrant held! Even your ten-thousand-foot white bull form cannot breach the Kunlun golden beam!'
Under combat escalation: extends golden diamond chains across the sky, anchoring the cosmic perimeter of the West.
Crucible roleplaying cue: Stands impassive as a mountain bastion, refusing parley or mortal bribery until Prince Nata accepts the beast's surrender.
npcs.notes: **Want:** Hold the west quarter from the Golden Beam Summit of Kunlun, the mountain where the fan's leaf was born. **Role:** Fourth guardian; his post is set by the personal order of the aged Buddha in the Great Thunderclap Monastery.
npcs.faction: The Heavenly and Buddhist Enforcement Host

quests.title: Borrow the Fan from Princess Iron-Fan
quests.name: Borrow the Fan from Princess Iron-Fan
quests.description: Travel to Palm-Leaf Cave to request the miraculous Palm-Leaf Fan from Princess Iron-Fan, navigating local tribute traditions and the matriarch's fierce hostility over her exiled son.

steps.title: Ask the householder for the fan's keeper
steps.text: Hear about the Immortal Iron-Fan, the ten-yearly tribute and the month's road to Jade Cloud Mountain.

steps.title: Meet the woodcutter and find the cave
steps.text: Learn that she is Rakshasi, wife of the Bull King, and follow the path east.

steps.title: Ask Rakshasi in person
steps.text: Bow, ask for the fan and accept her sword strokes. Each insult worsens her grudge.

steps.title: Force her to hand over a fan
steps.text: Enter her stomach and demand it; leave with the false fan.

quests.notes:
The travelers discover that eight hundred li of roaring fire bar their passage west. To cross, Sun Wukong must journey to Jade Cloud Mountain and convince the mountain matriarch, Princess Iron-Fan, to lend her treasure fan.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Wukong presents himself courteously at Palm-Leaf Cave, absorbs fifteen sword strikes upon his diamond-hard scalp without retaliation, and is fanned 84,000 li across the continent by Rakshasi's true fan. Fortified by the Wind-Arresting Elixir, he infiltrates her inner tea chamber as a mole cricket, enters her belly, and coerces her into handing over a fan—only to discover upon the burning slopes that she surrendered a deceptive blaze-magnifying counterfeit.

**What-If Crucible:**
Wukong refuses to invade Rakshasi's body from within, offering instead a solemn celestial oath to intercede with Bodhisattva Guanyin and reunite her with her consecrated son Red Boy.

**Immediate Dilemma:**
Rakshasi's maternal heart softens toward the pledge, but the sudden arrival of reports detailing the Bull King's luxurious desertion with the Fox Princess triggers bitter paranoia, threatening a lethal escalation.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
Pilgrim Party reputation with the Palm-Leaf Household shifts (+1 on honoring the sacred vow, -2 if broken). Rakshasi's Grudge tracker adjusts accordingly, while The Mountain's Heat ticks +1 as delays leave the fire unquenched.

quests.title: Eighty-Four Thousand Li: The Wind-Arresting Elixir
quests.name: Eighty-Four Thousand Li: The Wind-Arresting Elixir
quests.description: After being blasted 84,000 li across the continent by Princess Iron-Fan, Sun Wukong must descend upon Little Sumeru Temple and secure the sacred Wind-Arresting Elixir from Bodhisattva Lingji.

steps.title: Find the way down to the temple
steps.text: Follow the bells and be announced by the gate worker.

steps.title: Accept the elixir and the sewn bag
steps.text: Lingji sews the pellet under the collar. Its presence is recorded.

quests.notes:
Fanned into the cosmic stratosphere, Sun Wukong touches down outside the tranquil monastery of Mount Sumeru. Here, divine aid awaits to counter the primordial Yin force of Kunlun's leaf.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Recognizing the temple chimes, Wukong visits Bodhisattva Lingji, who reveals the true primordial nature of the Palm-Leaf Fan. Lingji bestows the Wind-Arresting Elixir in a silk sachet sewn under Wukong's collar, rendering his earthly viscera as unyielding as Mount Meru and granting absolute immunity to celestial gales.

**What-If Crucible:**
Wukong, stung in his warrior pride by the retreat, refuses the Bodhisattva's defensive talisman and insists on overpowering the storm winds through sheer physical mass and brute transformation.

**Immediate Dilemma:**
Lingji permits the Great Sage to test his hubris; Wukong returns to Jade Cloud Mountain unprotected and is violently blown across the world a second time, losing vital days while the pilgrims bake in the heat.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
Little Sumeru Temple standing shifts -1 for flouting holy guidance; Rakshasi's Grudge advances +1 as her victory hardens her resolve; The Mountain's Heat ticks +1 as another day is lost.

quests.title: Find King Powerful at the Cloud-Touching Cave
quests.name: Find King Powerful at the Cloud-Touching Cave
quests.description: Following the revelation of the false fan, seek out Sun Wukong's estranged sworn brother, the Bull Demon King, at the Cloud-Touching Cave on Hoard-Thunder Mountain to negotiate for the true relic.

steps.title: Learn who and where King Powerful is
steps.text: Local spirit's account: the brazier, the desertion, Hoard-Thunder 3,000 li south.

steps.title: Meet Jade Countenance in the pines
steps.text: Choose a lie or the truth; her reaction decides whether the Bull King comes out armed.

steps.title: Fight or parley with the Bull King
steps.text: The duel is drawn after over a hundred rounds.

quests.notes:
The Local Spirit of the Flames warns Wukong that the genuine fan can only be unlocked with the Bull Demon King's cooperation. Wukong travels three thousand li south to the demon lord's secondary estate.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Wukong confronts Princess Jade Countenance in the orchid forest, using intimidation to bring the Bull Demon King out in heavy martial armor. The two sworn brothers engage in a ferocious duel of cudgel against iron rod spanning over a hundred rounds, until an emissary from the Green Wave Dragon Lagoon pulls the Bull King away to an underwater feast.

**What-If Crucible:**
Wukong foregoes violent theatrics, greets the Bull King strictly as an honored elder brother with ceremonial wine, and diplomatically addresses his grievances over Red Boy.

**Immediate Dilemma:**
The Bull King is flattered and agrees to parley over a banquet, but demands that Wukong help conceal his double-marriage and enormous dowry from Rakshasi.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
Hoard-Thunder Court standing improves +1 initially, but collapses -2 when Wukong's subterfuge is uncovered; The Bull King's Pursuit countdown advances +1 as demon scouts mobilize.

quests.title: The Crab at the Green Wave Banquet
quests.name: The Crab at the Green Wave Banquet
quests.description: Infiltrate the opulent underwater dragon court at Green Wave Lagoon disguised as a water beast to track the Bull Demon King and hijack his golden-eyed steed.

steps.title: Follow the Bull King to the tablet
steps.text: Trail him to the stone tablet at Green Wave Lagoon.

steps.title: Enter the dragon palace as a crab
steps.text: Pass the gateway; the hall seizes you.

steps.title: Take the golden-eyed beast
steps.text: Slip out and untie it from beneath the arch. The Bull King will notice when the banquet ends.

quests.notes:
Pursuing the Bull King beneath the jade waters of Green Wave Lagoon, Wukong adopts an aquatic disguise to penetrate the draconic banquet hall without triggering a regional naval war.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Transforming into a thirty-six-pound river crab, Wukong slips past the coral palisades into the dragon palace, feigns humility when briefly snared by guards, observes the Bull King's drunken boastfulness, slips back to the palace gates, and commandeers the Water-Repellent Golden-Eyed Beast.

**What-If Crucible:**
The Old Dragon King detects Sun Wukong's golden gaze through the crab shell and formally toasts him before the assembly, forcing an open confrontation in the dragon throne room.

**Immediate Dilemma:**
Wukong must decide whether to brawl with his former aquatic allies and the Bull King simultaneously beneath deep water, or negotiate a joint alliance against the infernal mountain.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
Green Wave Lagoon Court standing falls -2; The Bull King departs early, advancing the Pursuit clock +2; Heavenly Host observers note the party's restraint.

quests.title: The Drunken Wife and the Seventh Red Thread
quests.name: The Drunken Wife and the Seventh Red Thread
quests.description: Infiltrate the Palm-Leaf Cave disguised as the Bull Demon King riding his captured beast, deceive Princess Iron-Fan during an intimate banquet, and extract the secret enlargement formula for the true fan.

steps.title: Enter the cave as the Bull King
steps.text: Ride the beast to the gate, claim to be the husband, be shown in.

steps.title: Pour wine and ask about the treasure
steps.text: Let Rakshasi drink; ask how so small a thing quenches eight hundred li.

steps.title: Take the fan and change back
steps.text: Leave through the door; the fan is now twelve feet long.

quests.notes:
Mounted on the Bull King's golden-eyed steed and transformed into his exact likeness, Sun Wukong returns to Jade Cloud Mountain to swindle the true fan from the grieving matriarch.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Rakshasi rejoices at her husband's apparent return, prepares wine, and laments the monkey's audacity. In her drunken affection, she spits the true fan from her tongue—an almond-leaf scaled to twelve feet by pressing the seventh red thread and reciting the Daoist mantra. Wukong unmasks himself, snatches the giant fan, and escapes, having forgotten to ask the shrinking formula.

**What-If Crucible:**
Wukong pushes his luck and presses Rakshasi for both the enlargement formula and the secret shrinking spell before seizing the fan.

**Immediate Dilemma:**
Rakshasi notices the simian gleam in his eyes at the second inquiry, screams for her armed maids, and hurls her frost-blue scimitars; Wukong keeps the fan at full size but is forced to fight his way through the household.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
Palm-Leaf Household standing drops -3; Rakshasi's Grudge advances +2; The Bull King's Pursuit ticks +1 as news of the defilement spreads.

quests.title: Break the Cloud-Touching Cave
quests.name: Break the Cloud-Touching Cave
quests.description: Lead Zhu Bajie and the mountain ghost auxiliaries in a nocturnal assault on the Cloud-Touching Cave to eliminate the Bull King's rear guard and shatter his secondary power base.

steps.title: Find Wukong at the cave
steps.text: Follow the spirit from the camp to Hoard-Thunder.

steps.title: Smash the cave door
steps.text: Break the door and meet the guard.

steps.title: Deal with Jade Countenance
steps.text: Kill her or spare her; the Bull King's reaction depends on it.

quests.notes:
As the Bull King pursues Wukong across the heavens, Tripitaka commands Zhu Bajie and the Local Spirit's spectral soldiers to assault the demon king's southern fortress.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Eight Rules and the ghost battalions storm Hoard-Thunder Mountain, smash the stone gates with the nine-pronged muckrake, repel over a hundred lance-wielding beast soldiers, slay the fox heiress Princess Jade Countenance, and reduce the cave complex to smoldering ash.

**What-If Crucible:**
Eight Rules stays his rake when Jade Countenance pleads for mercy, agreeing to spare the estate in exchange for her surrendering the Bull King's celestial treasury and storehouses.

**Immediate Dilemma:**
Sparing the fox heiress preserves regional wealth and reduces bloodshed, but leaves the Bull King with an intact fortress, fresh reinforcements, and a fortified redoubt to fall back upon.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
Hoard-Thunder Court standing remains salvageable (+1); The Bull King's Pursuit advances +2 as he fights with uncompromised territory; The Mountain's Heat ticks +1 as the siege prolongs.

quests.title: The Contest of Seven Transformations
quests.name: The Contest of Seven Transformations
quests.description: Engage the Bull Demon King in a relentless aerial battle of seventy-two transformations across mountain peaks, matching predator against prey in mythological shapeshifting warfare.

steps.title: Pursue the swan
steps.text: Turn into a vulture and strike.

steps.title: Trade transformations
steps.text: Out-change each creature: eagle, crane, deer, leopard, bear.

steps.title: Meet the white bull
steps.text: Grow to match and swing the rod.

quests.notes:
Deprived of his weapons and beasts, the enraged Bull King takes flight, triggering an epic high-altitude contest of dynamic animal transformations against Sun Wukong.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Wukong counters the Bull King form for form—hawk against swan, eagle against vulture, phoenix against crane, tiger against deer, and leopard against lion—until the Bull King reveals his primordial form: an colossal white bull ten thousand feet long. Wukong scales his avatar to one hundred thousand feet before the Heavenly Host closes the sky.

**What-If Crucible:**
Wukong breaks off the shapeshifting duel midway and appeals to their five-hundred-year-old pact as the Seven Great Sages of Mount Huaguo, offering an armistice.

**Immediate Dilemma:**
The Bull King, emotionally shaken by memories of their ancient brotherhood, hesitates between his oath and his fury, demanding that Heaven withdraw its net first.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
Hoard-Thunder Court standing rises +2; Heavenly Host standing drops -2 as celestial generals view the hesitation as insubordination; The Mountain's Heat advances +2 during the standstill.

quests.title: The Net of Heaven and Earth
quests.name: The Net of Heaven and Earth
quests.description: Coordinate with Devaraja Li, Prince Nata, and the Four Diamond Guardians to encircle Jade Cloud Mountain with celestial cosmic nets and force the Bull Demon King's unconditional surrender.

steps.title: Close the four quarters
steps.text: Each Diamond Guardian takes a post.

steps.title: Block the sky and break the bull's heads
steps.text: Nata cuts, the heads regrow, and the fiery wheel and mirror take over.

steps.title: Take the surrender at the cave
steps.text: Lead the roped bull to the Palm-Leaf Cave and demand the fan.

quests.notes:
The Jade Emperor and Sakyamuni Buddha dispatch cosmic forces to seal all four quarters of Heaven and Earth, hemming in the rampaging white bull.

**Canonical Outcome:**
The Four Diamond Guardians lock the north, south, east, and west horizons. Devaraja Li trains the demon-reflecting mirror from the zenith while Prince Nata manifests three heads and six arms, beheads the bull repeatedly with his fire wheel, ropes its nostrils, and forces its surrender. Rakshasi emerges from Palm-Leaf Cave in nun's robes to present the true fan.

**What-If Crucible:**
Wukong requests that Prince Nata and the celestial hosts hold their fire, allowing him to subdue the Bull King without humiliating him before the Four Guardians.

**Immediate Dilemma:**
The Bull King exploits the opening in the celestial cordon to break eastward, wounding several divine foot-soldiers before being pinned against the mountain rim.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
Heavenly Host standing drops -3 for compromising discipline; Cosmic Net clock suffers a setback of -2; The Bull King's Pursuit reaches its violent climax.

quests.title: Forty-Nine Waves
quests.name: Forty-Nine Waves
quests.description: Perform the sacred forty-nine wave ritual with the True Palm-Leaf Fan to permanently extinguish the underground coal-fires of the Flaming Mountains and bring fertility to the western desert.

steps.title: Ask Rakshasi how to end the fire
steps.text: She tells you: forty-nine waves.

steps.title: Fan the mountain forty-nine times
steps.text: Rain falls only where fire burned.

steps.title: Return the fan
steps.text: Give it back at dawn; Rakshasi shrinks it and leaves.

quests.notes:
With the Bull King in celestial custody and Princess Iron-Fan humbled, Sun Wukong must execute the full ritual to break the fiery curse forever.

**Canonical Outcome:**
Rakshasi reveals that while three waves bring temporary rain, forty-nine consecutive waves permanently eradicate the underground fire. Wukong waves the fan forty-nine times; gentle rain drenches the scorched valley without wetting the travelers, green shoots sprout from the ash, and the fan is returned to Rakshasi as she departs for solitary Taoist cultivation.

**What-If Crucible:**
Zhu Eight Rules urges the party to confiscate the fan permanently or sell it to the Red-Brick villagers to guarantee endless tribute and feast food along their road.

**Immediate Dilemma:**
Keeping the artifact ensures the pilgrims possess a devastating tactical superweapon, but leaves the local populace dependent on mortal greed and breaks their Buddhist vows.

**Long-Term Campaign Ripple:**
Pilgrim Party reputation collapses with all local households (-3); The Fire's Return clock is permanently disabled; The Mountain's Heat resets to 0.

items.name: The True Palm-Leaf Fan
items.specs: Stowed size: almond-leaf, carried in the mouth. Enlarged size: 12 ft, wrapped in 36 plaited red threads. Activation: left thumb on the 7th red thread plus the formula Hui-xu-he-xi-xi-chui-hu. Per wave: 1 = fire out, 2 = cool breeze, 3 = rain on burnt ground only. Fanned at a creature: drift of 84,000 li. Permanent quench of the mountain: 49 waves. Counter: Wind-Arresting Elixir. Shrink formula is a separate oral secret.
items.notes: A leaf of the supreme yin begotten of Heaven and Earth at the back of Mount Kunlun when chaos divided (Lingji). The villagers call its keeper Immortal Iron-Fan; the Bull King and Rakshasi both know how to enlarge and shrink it. Wukong learns only half the method and cannot shrink it.

items.name: The False Palm-Leaf Fan
items.specs: Looks like a standard palm-leaf fan. Waved at the Mountain of Flames: wave 1 makes the blaze brighter, wave 2 makes it a hundredfold fiercer, wave 3 sends flames ten thousand feet high. The text shows no creature-blowing effect and no enlarge or shrink function for it.
items.notes: Handed to Wukong when he bargains for his release from inside Rakshasi. Wukong carries it back, burns the hair off both thighs testing it, and throws it by the road, where the mountain spirit picks it up and recognises it. Rakshasi later laughs that it was only given to get him away.

items.name: Wind-Arresting Elixir
items.specs: One pellet in a tiny silk bag. Sewn under the collar it is stored; held in the mouth and swallowed it takes effect: viscera become firm, skin and bones fortified. Immunity to the True Palm-Leaf Fan's drift, any number of waves. Single use. Not used by Lingji before the Tang Monk's journey.
items.notes: Received by Lingji from Tathagata along with the Flying-Dragon Staff. Wukong sews it into his collar at Little Sumeru, then swallows it unawares when he turns into a mole cricket and enters Rakshasi; that is why the Bull King cannot move him with the fan later.

items.name: Flying-Dragon Staff
items.specs: Bodhisattva Relic Weapon (Divine Gilded Rattan Staff) | Damage: Subdue Fiend | Reach: 7 ft | Special: Transmutes upon command into an eight-clawed golden dragon that constricts and paralyzes airborne storm fiends and wind demons.
items.notes: A sacred golden staff bestowed upon Bodhisattva Lingji by Tathagata Buddha on Mount Sumeru. Carved with coiling cloud-dragons, it served as the decisive instrument that bound and subdued the Yellow Wind Demon in the western borderlands.

items.name: Golden-Hooped Rod
items.specs: Stowed behind the ear as a needle; one shake grows it to bowl-thick. At "Grow!" it scales with Wukong to 100,000 ft. Fought the Bull King's cast-iron rod to a draw over 100 rounds, twice. Rakshasi's blue blades, 10 to 15 strokes to the head, did no damage to its owner.
items.notes: The As-You-Will Gold-Banded Cudgel (Ruyi Jingu Bang), forged of divine black iron and banded with dual golden rings. Originating as the sea-settling anchor needle of the Eastern Ocean Dragon King, it obeys Sun Wukong's mental command alone, scaling effortlessly from an embroidery needle behind the ear to a cosmic pillar bridging Heaven and Earth.

items.name: Eight Rules' Nine-Pronged Muckrake
items.specs: Nine pointed prongs. A hit leaves nine bloody holes. Smashes cave doors and door ledges in one blow (Cloud-Touching Cave, Palm-Leaf Cave). Killed Princess Jade Countenance with one strike. Carried on the shoulder.
items.notes: The nine-pronged treasure muckrake forged of divine cold-iron by Laozi and bestowed upon Zhu Bajie during his tenure as Marshal of the Heavenly Reeds. Embodying the elemental resonance of Wood, its brutal spikes shatter solid stone doorways, blast reinforced iron gates, and leave nine lethal puncture wounds.

items.name: The Bull King's Cast-Iron Rod
items.specs: Cast-iron bar wielded one-handed by the Bull King in humanoid form. Matched the golden-hooped rod for over 100 rounds on Hoard-Thunder Mountain. Dropped, with his armour, when he flees as a swan; he is then forced to use his wife's swords.
items.notes: He picks it up on hearing a noise at his cave door. It is not at the Palm-Leaf Cave when he returns there in a hurry, so he takes Rakshasi's blue swords instead.

items.name: The Two Blue-Bladed Treasure Swords
items.specs: Matched Pair (Dual Frost-Blue Dao Scimitars) | Damage: Slashing / Cleaving | Speed: Swift Dual-Wield | Weight: 14 lbs combined | Durability: High Divine Steel.
items.notes: A pair of razor-sharp, blue-steel scimitars carried by Princess Iron-Fan when defending the Palm-Leaf Cave. Though incapable of piercing Sun Wukong's diamond-hard skull, they are wielded with blistering speed by both Rakshasi and the Bull Demon King in close combat.

items.name: Nata's Monster-Cleaving Sword
items.specs: Wielded in the three-headed, six-armed form. Strikes the neck of the white-bull form; each beheading is followed by a new head within moments, more than ten times in the same fight.
items.notes: Nata cuts first from the bull's back. The endless regrowth is what makes him bring out the fiery wheel and rope instead of continuing to cut.

items.name: Nata's Fiery Wheel
items.specs: Hung on a horn, it ignites true immortal fire that burns the whole beast. The target roars and thrashes, but cannot shake it off while the mirror holds its shape.
items.notes: Used after the beheadings fail. Combined with the mirror, it is what forces the Bull King to plead "I'm willing to make submission to Buddhism".

items.name: Nata's Monster-Tying Rope
items.specs: Drapes round the neck and threads through the nostrils of a captured monster so it can be led by hand. Holds a bull the size of a mountain (10,000 ft long, 800 ft high).
items.notes: Applied after the Bull King surrenders. Pilgrim then gathers the entire host and leads the bull to the Palm-Leaf Cave to demand the fan.

items.name: The Imp-Reflecting Mirror
items.specs: When trained on a shapeshifter it pins the creature in its original form: it cannot change out of that shape. Range: line of sight in the open air.
items.notes: Devaraja Li trains it on the bull while Nata ties it. The Bull King had changed into the white bull to gore Li; the mirror turns that last transformation into his prison.

trackers.name: The Mountain's Heat
trackers.notes: Ticks +1 each time the party fans the fire with the false fan, enters the flames unprotected or spends a day idle at the camp. Ticks -1 when a true-fan wave is made. At 8, the fire pushes the camp back.

consequences.description: The blaze doubles in height. Sha Monk's feet and the horse are scorched; travel on the burnt road to the camp costs a day.
The fire reaches the Fire-Line Camp. The party must retreat twenty li to the village.

trackers.name: Rakshasi's Grudge
trackers.notes: Ticks +1 for each insult to Rakshasi (naming Red Boy, entering her body, impersonating her husband). Ticks -1 for each offer to bring Red Boy to see her. At 3 she fans Wukong away; at 6 she shuts her household to all callers.

consequences.description: Rakshasi fans Wukong with the true fan. Without the elixir he drifts 84,000 li and lands at Little Sumeru.
She bars the gate and the household turns every caller away; the maid is moved to the hall for protection.

trackers.name: The Bull King's Pursuit
trackers.notes: Starts when the true fan is taken from the Palm-Leaf Cave. Ticks +1 per hour of the shen watch spent without the fan in the party's hands. At 4 the Bull King recovers the beast and rides to the Palm-Leaf Cave. At 6 he flees there again after the transformation contest.

consequences.description: The Bull King finds the beast gone, guesses who took it and rides to the Palm-Leaf Cave in a rage.
Defeated in the sky above Hoard-Thunder, the Bull King retreats to the Palm-Leaf Cave. The Heavenly host takes post at the cave gate.

trackers.name: The Net of Heaven and Earth
trackers.notes: Ticks +1 for each quarter held by a Diamond Guardian (north, south, east, west). At 4 the net is complete and the Bull King's way out is closed on all sides.

consequences.description: North and south posts hold. The Bull King can only flee east or west.
The net is complete. Devaraja Li and Prince Nata take position over Jade Cloud Mountain.

trackers.name: The Fire's Return
trackers.notes: One tick per month after a one-wave quench. At 12 the fire starts again unless the mountain has been fanned 49 times. Ticks -12 (resets to 0 permanently) when 49 waves are done.

consequences.description: Early crops rise; the villagers tell the party that the rain will only last a year.
The fire returns. The local spirit and the households must beg another audience with the fan keeper.

factions.name: The Tang Pilgrim Party
factions.doctrine: Seek scriptures in the Western Heaven. The mission is under imperial commission of the Great Tang and Buddhist protection; the master never turns aside from the West, so the disciples must find a way through whatever blocks the road.
resourcesControlled: Official travel rescript of the Great Tang
Protection decreed by the Buddha for the journey
factions.description: Four travellers bound by vow: a monk, an ape, a boar and a river spirit. Their solidarity is high, their wealth is almost nil, and their one coercive tool is Wukong.
factions.notes: S+3 because the four are bound by oath and common labour. E-2 because they live on alms and borrowed hospitality. C+1 because the party has no authority except the Buddhist decree but can fight any local power. Quadrant Clan (+S,-E).

factions.name: The Households of the Mountain of Flames and the Local Spirit Office
factions.type: Agrarian Villages under a Tutelary Spirit
factions.doctrine: The region has no seasons; all four are hot. Grain depends on the fan: a decennial pilgrimage to Jade Cloud Mountain with four hogs, four sheep, rare flowers and fruit, fowl and wine. Households bathe ritually before going up. A mountain spirit watches the fire.
resourcesControlled: Rice-pudding flour sourced through the fan's rains
The ghost soldiers under the local spirit
factions.description: Families who farm only when the fan comes. They have no army, no formal governor, and one deity whom Laozi exiled here.
factions.notes: S+3 from shared tribute and shared fate. E-3 because nothing grows without the fan. C-2 because there is no ruler: the householder only asks the party in for tea. Quadrant Clan.

factions.name: The Palm-Leaf Cave Household
factions.doctrine: A strict household of self-cultivation with no male inside, not even a baby boy. Its wealth is the fan, which it never lends 'lightly'. It holds a long grievance against the one who 'ensnared' its son.
resourcesControlled: Decennial tribute from the Mountain of Flames villages
factions.description: Rakshasi, her maids and the cave. The household controls rain and cool air across the whole Mountain of Flames region.
factions.notes: S+2 (kin and loyalty, closed), E-1 (rural, self-sufficient; income comes from rare tribute), C+2 (fan and swords). Quadrant Clan.

factions.name: The Hoard-Thunder Court of the Bull Demon King
factions.doctrine: A fox king's vast fortune was given as dowry so that Jade Countenance could take the Bull King in as consort. In return he gives protection and a name. The cave keeps a hundred-plus armed guards and a library of elixir books.
resourcesControlled: Over a hundred armed guards of beast-spirits
factions.description: A household bought with a dowry. It supplies jewels, silk, firewood and rice to the first wife through a standing arrangement.
factions.notes: S-1 (transactional marriage, no kin), E+4 (vast fortune), C+2 (armed guards). Quadrant Market (-S,+E).

factions.name: The Green Wave Lagoon Court
factions.doctrine: A courtly society of dragon-kin, perch ladies, crab and shrimp attendants. A banquet is the unit of politics: guests are judged by etiquette, and breaches draw a sentence of flogging.
resourcesControlled: Dry jewelled hall under the lagoon
Banquet stores of the eight treasure dainties
factions.description: Ceremonial but permeable; a disguised crab can enter on the strength of a doggerel lyric and an apology.
factions.notes: S+2 (extended dragon family), E+3 (jewelled hall, treasury), C+1 (flogging as formal sanction). Quadrant Adhocracy (+S,+E).

factions.name: The Heavenly and Buddhist Enforcement Host
factions.doctrine: No god dares withhold protection from the scripture journey. Tathagata's secret command and the Jade Emperor's decree mobilise the Four Diamond Guardians, the Six Gods of Darkness and Light, the Eighteen Guardians of Monasteries and the Heavenly King's troops.
resourcesControlled: Cosmic nets at the four quarters
Decrees from Tathagata and the Jade Emperor
factions.description: A chain of command with guardian posts on four peaks. It acts only after Tathagata's memorial reaches the Jade Emperor.
factions.notes: S-2 (rank over solidarity), E-1 (paid in merit, not coin), C+4 (decree-backed arrest power). Quadrant Hierarchy (-S,-E).

factions.name: The Little Sumeru Temple
factions.doctrine: Preserve the instruments Tathagata entrusted: the staff and the elixir. They are used only in service of the journey. Hospitality is brief: 'there's not time for me to entertain you'.
factions.description: A single Bodhisattva's mountain with a gate, a throne and a few workers.
factions.notes: S-1 (a single hierarch), E-2 (monastic poverty), C+2 (Tathagata's staff). Quadrant Hierarchy.

creatures.name: The Great White Bull (Bull Demon King, true form)
creatures.summary: A white bull ten thousand feet from head to toe and eight hundred high at the shoulder, with horns like iron pagodas and teeth like daggers. It is the Bull Demon King's last transformation, kept after six animal disguises fail.

senses.blindspots: Eyes 'like bolts of lightning' track a single large foe poorly when many gods close from different quarters.

defenses.armorType: Dark tendonous hide and flinty horns
resistances: bladed weapons (new head grows after each beheading)

disposition.ethologySummary: Solitary (S:1), Active Ranging Hunter (E:3), Adaptive Instinct (C:2)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: While the bull fills the sky, travellers on the Hoard-Thunder and Jade Cloud roads refuse to move; the villagers close their doors and the rains stop being sought.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Stop at the first cue that tells it whether to fight or flee.

cues.label: Is a divine host or Heaven's net in view?
Does the foe match its size?
Is the foe smaller and alone?

defaultExit.label: Bellow and wait for a gap

signatureActions.name: Seven-form escape
signatureActions.trigger: Pressed in a duel by the Great Sage
signatureActions.effect: Cycles swan, eagle, crane, deer, leopard, bear in turn before taking bull form.

signatureActions.name: Horn charge
signatureActions.effect: Two flinty horns gore through armour.

signatureActions.name: Regrowing head
signatureActions.effect: A new head grows each time, breathing black air and shining gold from the eyes.

instinctiveQuirks: Refuses to yield the fan out of hatred, not need
Reverts to bull form under strain
spoorAndSigns: Wind-blown trees along the mountain ridge
Burnt armour left on a path
psychologyAndFolklore.vocalizations: A bellow that shakes ridges and mountains
psychologyAndFolklore.vernacularFolklore: Villagers say the fan and the bull were the same quarrel from the start; a wife and a concubine and a monkey made the hills ring.

creatures.name: The Water-Repellent Golden-Eyed Beast
creatures.subtype: War mount of the Bull King
creatures.summary: A carved-saddle mount with golden eyes whose coat repels water, so it can wait dry inside a lagoon palace's gate. It carries the Bull King, then Wukong in disguise, between Hoard-Thunder, Green Wave and the Palm-Leaf Cave.

disposition.ethologySummary: Mated Pair or Family (S:2), Local Grazer (E:2), Rigid Scripted Instinct (C:3)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: A loose mount means the Bull King is nearby and angry; households along the road to Jade Cloud lock their gates.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Obey the first rider who holds the reins confidently.

cues.label: Does the rider hold the reins and the saddle?
Is the Bull King's voice near?

signatureActions.name: Dry-gate wait
signatureActions.effect: Waits dry beside the lagoon's bottom gateway.

signatureActions.name: Cloud carry
signatureActions.trigger: Mounted by a rider with a command word
signatureActions.effect: Carries a rider from lagoon floor to cloud roads.

instinctiveQuirks: Accepts a rider's disguise without suspicion
spoorAndSigns: Water-beaded hoofprints that dry at once
psychologyAndFolklore.vernacularFolklore: Dragon-palace servants say the beast cannot be wet by any lake in the world.

creatures.name: The Beast-Spirits of the Cloud-Touching Cave
creatures.summary: More than a hundred spirits who walk as soldiers with lances and rods, but are in truth donkeys, asses, cows, stallions, badgers, foxes, musk deer, goats, tigers and antelopes.

senses.blindspots: A broken door and a burning cave scatter their discipline.

defenses.armorType: Quilted soldier's gear over animal hide

disposition.ethologySummary: Structured Pack (S:3), Local Grazer (E:2), Adaptive Instinct (C:2)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: A hundred spears at the door make a lone party withdraw; a party with allies faces only a nuisance.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Follow the guard captain's call to charge or flee.

cues.label: Is Jade Countenance or the Bull King ordering a sally?

signatureActions.name: Massed sally
signatureActions.effect: A hundred-plus soldiers pour out of the cave with lances and rods.

instinctiveQuirks: Revert to animal form when killed
spoorAndSigns: Hoof and paw prints around the cave mouth
psychologyAndFolklore.vocalizations: Shrill battle cries; animal grunts when killed.
psychologyAndFolklore.vernacularFolklore: Travellers say the Bull King's guards are 'a farm in armour'.

creatures.name: The Ghost Soldiers of the Flame-Mountain Spirit
creatures.subtype: Shade soldiery of a mountain office
creatures.summary: A band of ghost soldiers under the local spirit who bar the Bull King's retreat and sack the Cloud-Touching Cave alongside Eight Rules.

senses.blindspots: Obey only the local spirit's orders.

disposition.ethologySummary: Structured Pack (S:3), Passive Ambush (E:1), Rigid Scripted Instinct (C:3)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: Villagers are used to them; strangers on the road are watched but not harassed.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Do what the local spirit says.

cues.label: Has the local spirit given an order?
Is the Bull King in sight?

signatureActions.name: Barring the way
signatureActions.trigger: A fugitive tries to flee past them
signatureActions.effect: They form a line that blocks the road.

spoorAndSigns: Cold patches in the hot air
psychologyAndFolklore.vernacularFolklore: Households say the spirit's soldiers keep the fire from reaching the grain.

creatures.name: The Courtiers of the Green Wave Lagoon
creatures.summary: Dragon sons and daughters, perch ladies, crabs, whales and iguana drummers who staff the Old Dragon King's banquet. They seize intruders on command and sentence them to flogging.

senses.blindspots: A courtier's verse can lower the court's guard.

disposition.ethologySummary: Structured Pack (S:3), Active Ranging Hunter (E:3), Adaptive Instinct (C:2)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: A banquet at the lagoon closes the Scattered-Rocks route to ordinary travellers while the court is in session.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Tally breaches of etiquette; flog at three.

cues.label: Does the stranger bear a rank the court knows?
Did a courtier plead for the stranger?

signatureActions.name: Seize the wild crab
signatureActions.trigger: A stranger enters the banquet hall
signatureActions.effect: Dragon sons surge forward and grab the intruder.

psychologyAndFolklore.vocalizations: Court music, whale squeals and drumbeats.
psychologyAndFolklore.vernacularFolklore: Fishers say a banquet at the lagoon lasts as long as the Bull King wants it to.

creatures.name: Tigers and Wolves of the Jade Cloud Road
creatures.summary: The householder warns that the long road to Jade Cloud Mountain has no habitation and 'plenty of tigers and wolves'.

disposition.ethologySummary: Mated Pair or Family (S:2), Active Ranging Hunter (E:3), Feral and Chaotic (C:1)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: Without an armed escort, the month-long walk to Jade Cloud is refused by the villagers.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Attack the first lone traveller; stay clear of fire.

cues.label: Is the traveller alone and unarmed?
Is there fire or a large party?

defaultExit.label: Trail the party at a distance

signatureActions.name: Roadside ambush
signatureActions.trigger: A lone traveller on the road

spoorAndSigns: Paw prints on the dry roadside
psychologyAndFolklore.vernacularFolklore: Villagers say the road to Jade Cloud is longer on the way back.
